events.label: ISM Manufacturing PMI June 2026 — ACTUAL: 54.0 (37-month high; beat consensus 53.0)
events.note: June ISM Manufacturing printed 54.0 — 37-month high; 6th consecutive month above 50; beat consensus 53.0. Bull case from June 30 night brief (25% probability, ISM >52) triggered. SPX cleared 7,460 regime gate intraday for first time in 9 sessions. 10Y yield rose +10bps to 4.47% on the inflationary read (Prices Paid sub-index was 82.1 in May). Flash S&P Global PMI was 55.7 — official ISM slightly below but still at 37-month high. Manufacturing expansion has run 6 consecutive months; AI capex cycle and Iran stand-down supply chain normalization confirmed.

events.label: June Non-Farm Payrolls 8:30 AM ET — consensus ~100K (vs. May 172K revised); markets open
events.note: June employment report. REVISED consensus: ~100K (Capital Economics: 130K) — sharp deceleration from May's 172K revised. ADP May was 122K; preliminary June weekly run-rate ~123K implied. THREE SCENARIOS: (1) STRONG (>150K, wages +0.4%) = BofA three-hike path (Sep/Oct/Dec 2026) locked in over 3-day unhedgeable July 4 gap; DXY spikes; SPX gaps lower July 7 — HOLD degrades to STEP ASIDE/BEARISH. (2) GOLDILOCKS (90–130K, wages +0.2%) = regime confirms; BUY upgrade viable for July 7; GOOGL long expands; NVDA re-entry window opens if SPX >7,460 + VIX <17 on July 7. (3) WEAK (<90K, wages flat) = recession fears emerge; TLT long pays; growth tech faces further selling. Markets closed July 3 — NFP reaction prints into a 3-day weekend gap; no ability to hedge July 3–6.

events.label: TSLA Q2 2026 deliveries report (est. 396,500–420,000 vehicles)
events.note: Tesla Q2 2026 delivery report lands same morning as June NFP. Consensus range: 396,500–420,000 vehicles. Beat = constructive for TSLA and EV sentiment; miss alongside a strong NFP = double negative for July 7 open. Musk 'trillionaire restoration' from June 29 (SpaceX/TSLA) already in the price; delivery beat needed to sustain above $420. Watch for gross margin commentary (any hints via production data).

events.label: US Market Holiday — Independence Day observed (July 4 falls on Saturday)
events.note: US equity markets closed Friday July 3 as July 4, 2026 falls on a Saturday. 3-day weekend gap (July 3–6). The June NFP report prints Thursday July 2 — any repricing accumulates over the full 3-day gap before July 7 open. Use July 2 close as the last chance to hedge or reduce before the gap.

events.label: SPCX added to Nasdaq-100 Index — ~$4.3B forced passive inflows from QQQ/QQQM; post-NFP holiday return
events.note: Dual catalyst day: (1) SPCX (SpaceX) inclusion in Nasdaq-100 effective July 7 — QQQ/QQQM forced to buy ~$4.3B of SPCX at index weight. Mechanical passive-flow catalyst. ISM 54.0 and manufacturing expansion are constructive for launch infrastructure demand. (2) July 7 open reflects the full NFP repricing accumulated over the July 4 3-day gap — if NFP was strong, gap-down; if Goldilocks, potential gap-up into earnings season. Two simultaneous catalysts (NFP repricing + SPCX passive flow) create higher-than-normal volatility. NVDA re-entry window opens IF SPX >7,460 AND VIX <17 simultaneously AND NVDA >$200 on volume. GOOGL and META pre-earnings buildup begins.

events.label: FOMC Minutes from June 17 meeting (est.) — first post-dot-plot-removal release
events.note: Minutes from the June 17 FOMC meeting (est. release ~3 weeks after meeting). First FOMC at which Warsh removed the dot plot. SCOTUS upheld Fed independence June 29 — minutes will reveal the internal rate debate with full institutional certainty now restored. ISM 54.0 July 1 (37-month high) provides hawkish data context — the June 17 committee had May ISM of 54.0 too; unanimous hawkish tone = BofA 3-hike forecast solidified. Any dissent or hike-pause language = dovish surprise and rate relief. Key input for Q3 positioning heading into the July 14 CPI print.

events.label: SK Hynix ADR Nasdaq listing — $29.4B offering, 17.79M shares (potentially largest ADR in history)
events.note: SK Hynix Nasdaq ADR listing — $29.4B offering (17.79M shares). Underwriters: BofA, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, JPMorgan. ISM 54.0 (July 1) confirms the manufacturing/AI capex cycle that underpins HBM4 demand — constructive for ADR pricing. TSM +1% on July 1 ISM day is a positive read-through. Underwriter stabilization mandate (BofA/Goldman/Citigroup/JPMorgan) provides ADR floor support. HBM4 demand thesis: NVDA H200/B100 requires SK Hynix as primary supplier; ADR is first US capital markets clearing of that thesis. TSM, AVGO, NVDA read-through is constructive if ADR prices above consensus.

events.label: June CPI release (est.) — most important inflation data of the summer
events.note: June CPI is the next major inflation recalibration after May PCE (June 25, 4.1% YoY). US-Iran stand-down confirmed June 29 — Brent at $72–73/bbl, Hormuz normalization intact. ISM 54.0 with high Prices Paid (May: 82.1) raises risk of sticky goods inflation even as energy deflates. June CPI captures the first full month of Iran peace normalization. If CPI falls to 3.5% or below, the BofA 3-hike framework weakens and July 28 FOMC hike probability collapses. If CPI holds at 4.0%+, September hike is locked in. July 14 is the critical regime-reset date for H2 2026 positioning.

events.label: FOMC meeting (July 28-29) — rate hike on the table
events.note: Nine of 18 FOMC officials projected at least one 2026 rate hike at the June 17 meeting (Warsh's first as Chair). BofA calls for three hikes (Sep/Oct/Dec). ISM 54.0 (July 1, 37-month high) combined with high Prices Paid validates the hawkish case. A 25-bps hike (3.50–3.75% → 3.75–4.00%) at this meeting is a non-trivial probability if June CPI (~July 14) disappoints. SCOTUS upheld Fed independence June 29 — Warsh can hike without political interference. June CPI (~July 14) is the primary input.

events.label: Iran-US Islamabad Declaration 60-day deadline — Hormuz full reopening + sanctions relief
events.note: Deal operational from June 18 MOU signing; 60-day window expires August 13. June 29 US-Iran 'stand down' confirmed — both sides agreed to halt tit-for-tat attacks ahead of technical talks. Brent at $72.25 (July 1), Hormuz normalization proceeding. If August 13 deadline met with full Hormuz clearance, WTI could extend to $65–67 — extend XLE short and exit TBT. Failure = oil spike reversal and energy re-rally. The oil-crash pace is ahead of schedule relative to the original June 18 MOU framework.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since the June 12 IPO. SPCX confirmed in Russell 1000 and Nasdaq-100 (effective July 7). Capital structure: $75B IPO + $60B xAI acquisition + $20B bond offering = $155B in obligations. First earnings (Starlink subscriber/ARR growth, Starship launch cadence, cash burn rate) is the fundamental clearing event for re-entry. Two consecutive closes above $185 on above-average volume required before re-entry from current ~$153 range.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs; the $20B bond offering (June 22) already changed the capital structure risk profile — the lock-up expiry adds equity supply overhang on top. Exact date pending the prospectus's stated terms.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off -13% on the delay. Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst and adds uncertainty to AI infrastructure spending trajectories. Monitor for filing date announcement as a potential AI sentiment catalyst. Date is approximate placeholder for H1 2027 window.
